## What this is

TakwimuBridge is a qualitative data analysis (QDA) tool designed by **Sustainable Solutions Tanzania (SST)** for researchers, students, consultants, institutions and organizations working with Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), individual interviews, open-ended survey responses, and other textual qualitative data.

This build implements SST's own **Version 1.0 (MVP) workflow**: upload a transcript → identify the respondent/source → read → highlight → code → assign a colour → optionally score importance 1–10 → automatically count → compare respondents/themes → retrieve quotations → generate charts/word cloud → export results.

## Where your data is kept

Every project, source, code and coded reference you create is stored in your web browser's local storage, on your own device — that copy is the one you work on, so the tool stays fast and keeps working offline. All analysis runs in your browser.

**With an account.** When accounts are switched on for this site (look for **Sign in to sync** at the bottom of the sidebar), signing in also keeps each of your projects in your TakwimuBridge account, held in a cloud database (Supabase), so you can sign in on another computer and carry on where you left off. Your projects are private to you: the database only ever returns a researcher's own projects. If the same project is changed on two computers before they sync, nothing is overwritten — the other version is kept as a separate "conflicted copy". Signing out removes your projects from that browser, which matters on shared computers.

**Without an account**, everything stays in this browser only: clearing your browser's site data, using a different browser, or switching computers means your projects won't be there. Use **Export → Full Project Backup (JSON)** to move a project by hand.

Interview transcripts can contain personal information. Before storing real data in an account, check that this fits your consent forms and data-protection obligations (for example Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act).

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Highlighting, coding, theming, weighting | ✅ Real — genuinely computed, not mocked |
| Coding one passage to several theme groups (e.g. a cause, a challenge and an impact) in one reading | ✅ Real |
| Frequency, coverage, weighted-score, average-weight analysis, at theme, sub-theme or code level | ✅ Real — recalculated live from your actual coded data |
| Charts, heat map, theme cloud, word frequency, word cloud | ✅ Real — rendered client-side from your data |
| CSV / Excel / Word-report / image / JSON export | ✅ Real — generated client-side, downloads directly |
| DOCX / TXT / CSV import | ✅ Real — parsed client-side (mammoth.js / SheetJS); nothing is uploaded anywhere |
| Cross-device access | ✅ With an account — sign in on any computer. Without one, move projects with **Export → Full Project Backup (JSON)** |
| Multi-user projects / team coding | ❌ Not implemented — each account holds one researcher's own projects |
| Inter-coder reliability, advanced compound queries, codebooks-as-templates | ❌ Not implemented in v1 — the data model anticipates them (see below) but no UI yet |

## What later versions could add

Per SST's own functional description, later versions could add: codebooks as reusable templates, inter-coder reliability checks, team/multi-user projects with shared codebooks, more advanced compound queries ("Pollution AND Weak Enforcement", or "Pollution among District A respondents"), relationship/network maps between codes, and more sophisticated FGD speaker-level analysis. AI-suggested codes, which the researcher accepts or rejects like proofreading, are planned next. The data model here (themes with a parent/child hierarchy, and codings that can carry multiple theme IDs) is deliberately structured so those features can be added without a redesign.

## A naming note

This product's real name, **"TakwimuBridge"**, comes directly from SST's own functional description document. A separate, unrelated project in this workspace — a socio-economic **data catalog** site for university students — currently uses **"Takwimu Bridge"** (with a space) as an explicitly-labelled *placeholder* name, chosen before this product existed. If both are meant to be part of one product family, or if the data-catalog site's placeholder should be renamed to avoid confusion, that's a decision for the project owner — it hasn't been resolved here.
